basics.name: Rae (Ruiyan) Huang
basics.summary: Machine learning researcher building models for sequence and unstructured data: scientific LLMs, time-series forecasting, and user modeling. Experience designing training pipelines, running controlled experiments on model behavior, and shipping reproducible ML code.

work.name: Stanford SALT Lab (Prof. Diyi Yang)
work.summary: Extends general user modeling methods to multi-user interaction settings.
highlights: Implementing the General User Models (GUM) baseline and extending it from single-user to dyadic settings.
Modeling shared intent and coordination patterns from multi-user interaction traces.

work.name: van Dijk Lab, Yale
work.summary: Builds fine-tuning and evaluation pipelines for scientific language models on DNA methylation literature.
highlights: Designed a two-stage fine-tuning pipeline (summarization + QA) for Qwen3-1.7B on a DNA methylation benchmark; improved accuracy from 48% to 74% and outperformed substantially larger baseline LLMs.

Built data pipelines transforming unstructured scientific literature into structured QA datasets; designed a 400-question evaluation framework to systematically compare model variants and surface failure modes.
Translated evaluation results into model design decisions and communicated findings to mixed audiences through a research poster, technical writeups, and lab presentations.

work.name: Carbon Containment Lab
work.summary: Built long-horizon forecasting and scenario models for cooling-related energy demand and emissions.
highlights: Built a long-horizon time-series forecasting model (2020-2060) for cooling-related energy demand and emissions across U.S. and China real estate portfolios.

Integrated multi-source heterogeneous data, including climate projections, building characteristics, and technology adoption curves, into a unified modeling pipeline; defined modeling assumptions under uncertainty.
Designed scenario and sensitivity analyses to identify key drivers; produced decision-oriented dashboards used by LVMH and CBRE stakeholders.

work.name: Shan Shui Conservation Center
work.summary: Built the foundation of a wildlife re-identification pipeline for unstructured field imagery.
highlights: Built the foundation of China's first wildlife re-identification pipeline using embedding-based image matching on a custom database of unstructured field imagery.
Developed a top-k candidate retrieval tool and characterized failure modes, including visually similar individuals and lighting variation, to guide future model iterations.

education.area: Statistics & Data Science; minor in Climate Sciences and Solutions

publications.name: Simulated triangulations and quivers on non-orientable surfaces
publications.summary: Independent graph theory research involving simulations and proofs for triangulations and quivers on non-orientable surfaces.

projects.name: Renewable Generation Forecasting
projects.summary: Built machine-learning baselines for renewable generation forecasting using weather and power data.
highlights: Evaluated model performance across temporal splits and feature sets.
Created reproducible forecasting analysis for energy-system use cases.

projects.name: Demand Response Case Study
projects.summary: Developed a data analysis workflow for demand-response strategy evaluation.
highlights: Produced reproducible code and visualizations for energy-system decision support.

projects.name: Geospatial Mapping with Supervised Machine Learning
projects.summary: Processed large-scale geospatial datasets in ArcGIS and R to classify ecological recovery patterns from abandoned oil wells.
highlights: Applied supervised learning and geospatial data processing to environmental recovery analysis.
